entities.summary: Marcus Valerius Publicola was a politician of the Roman Republic who played a pivotal role in shaping the destiny of Rome during the late 4th century BCE. Born into a prominent patrician family, Publicola's early life was marked by a fierce commitment to the Roman Republic's values and institutions. He rose to prominence as a skilled orator and military leader, serving as magister equitum under the dictator Gaius Sulpicius Peticus in 358 BC and as consul in 355 and 353 BC. Publicola's most notable achievement was his role in the expulsion of the last king of Rome, Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, which marked a significant turning point in the Roman Republic's transition from monarchy to republicanism. This event had far-reaching consequences, including the establishment of the Roman Senate and the creation of a system of governance that would shape Western politics for centuries to come. Publicola's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of Roman law, politics, and society. His commitment to the principles of the Roman Republic and his leadership in shaping its institutions continue to inspire historians and scholars today.
